content.text:
Done.

**Root cause** — `checkDependencies` in `lib/decorate.js:114` resolved dependency names only through `checkExistence`, which inspects the instance, its prototype and `props`. Properties assigned in the `Request`/`Reply` constructors (`body`, `id`, `params`, `query`, `log`, `raw`, `request`) live in `konstructor.instanceProperties`, so they fell through and threw `FST_ERR_DEC_MISSING_DEPENDENCY` — even though `hasRequestDecorator` reports them present and `decorateRequest` refuses to overwrite them. `hasInstanceProperty` was added in #6753 but only wired into `decorateConstructor`'s already-present guard and the two existence checks.

**Change** — one line:

```js
if (!checkExistence(instance, deps[i]) && !hasInstanceProperty(instance, deps[i])) {
```

`hasInstanceProperty` walks the `parent` chain, so it works inside encapsulated plugins. `decorate()` passes a plain Fastify instance with no `instanceProperties`, so the instance path returns `false` immediately; and since `checkExistence` runs first, ordinary decorator dependencies never reach the second lookup.

**Tests** — added 5 cases to `test/decorator-instance-properties.test.js`: full built-in sets for `Request` and `Reply` as dependencies, an encapsulated plugin, a mix of built-ins and user decorators, and a regression case asserting unknown deps still throw `FST_ERR_DEC_MISSING_DEPENDENCY` and that a `Reply` decorator depending on the `Request`-only `params` still throws.

Verified both directions: the 4 new positive tests fail with the fix reverted and pass with it; the whole file is 11/11 green. Nothing committed.

One thing I couldn't do: `npx eslint` on the two changed files needs approval in this sandbox, so lint is unverified — the diff follows the surrounding style, but you may want to run `npm run lint` yourself. I also limited the run to that one test file per your instruction, so I haven't exercised the broader decorator suites.
